correctness.rationale: The scaling identity is exact: with \(\rho_t(x)=t^{-n}\phi(-x/t)\), \(F=\partial_1^m\rho_t\), \(\rho_t\) converges to \(\delta_0\) in distributions, and \(F\) converges to \(\partial_1^m\delta_0\). The pointwise-zero statement follows from \(\phi\) being constant near zero and compactly supported. A change of variables gives the exponent \(n-(n+m)p\); its sign gives the exact threshold. No nonstandard lemma or numerical certificate is required.

originality.rationale: Graham 2008, pp. 496–497, records pointwise failure for \(\delta\prime_0\) with an even test function, so the bare pointwise obstruction is not claimed as new. Vindas–Estrada 2010, Theorem 2, proves support exclusion for local \(L^p\) boundedness only for \(p\ge1\) and uses weak-star compactness in \(L^1\). The inspected full texts do not state the exact \(n/(n+m)\) quasi-norm profile for the general phi-transform. The literature searches returned no matching implication. Residual risk: the scaling refinement may be folklore.
residual_risks: The scaling refinement may be folklore or derivable from standard approximate-identity calculations; the searches did not prove priority.
The result is only for the general compactly supported phi-transform and does not establish counterexamples for each specific Fourier-inversion summability method.
For fixed \(n\) and \(m\), the range \(n/(n+m)<p<1\) is not settled by this claim.

value.rationale: The exact dimension/order-dependent threshold quantifies when a point-supported singularity can evade pointwise support detection under a subunit-\(L^p\) quasi-norm. It gives a precise obstruction to any dimension-independent extension below one, while sharply delimiting what remains unresolved for a fixed dimension and for specific Fourier summability means.
